newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's CNMV issues new guidelines on derivatives.
newsitem.headline: Spain's CNMV issues new guidelines on derivatives.

text.p: Spain's CNMV stock market commission published new guidelines on Thursday aimed at increasing transparency in derivatives investments.
Under the new guidelines, which take effect on Friday, funds must notify investors if they invest in derivatives and describe the risks involved.
The funds will be obliged to present quarterly reports.
They must also state the objective of the derivatives investment (short covering, profitability, greater efficiency) and the limits on the risks.
Foreign mutual funds sold in Spain must send their investors a report on their products and translate all the material into Spanish, the CNMV said.
The guidelines also require fund managers to be well informed about risks involved in derivatives.
The guidelines also state the requirements in the event that general risk limits are exceeded.
